newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 14.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Friday's Daily Variety:

* General Electric's NBC struck an agreement in principle with Viacom's Paramount Network Television to renew the hit sitcom Frasier for three more years. The deal, struck Wednesday night, could be announced as early as Friday. According to industry sources, NBC has agreed to pay Paramount a lump sum of roughly $50 million to reduce the studio's deficit on the show as well as boost the license fee to more than $2 million per episode.

* French media giant Havas and British broadcaster Carlton Communications were two members of a European consortium looking to invest in Time Warner's New Line Cinema, sources said. That consortium, and another led by Chris-Craft Industries, are both said to be going through due diligence on the cinema.
* Walt Disney ABC president Bob Iger said on Thursday President Bill Clinton's request for free airtime for political candidates would meet stiff resistance from the broadcasting industry.
* Director George Wolfe would direct an off Broadway production of Macbeth starring Alex Baldwin next January and would direct a musical in Central Park this summer.
* MTM Worldwide Distribution let go its top executive, Chuck Larsen, and two other domestic salesmen, on Thursday.
* Actor-director-writer Ben Stiller signed an exclusive deal with Fox 2000, to write, direct and produce films.
* Arnold Schwarzenegger has signed with the William Morris Agency. The move had been anticipated since he left International Creative Management a month ago.
